732310203.text: #Hmph. Pale Floater, you could stand to learn from our Yasnapati and {M#his}{F#her} unflinching calm.

732310205.text: Exactly! Just looking at that big mass of... stuff over there is pretty scary already...

732310208.text: Such trivial trials! They pale in comparison to the sacrifice that I must offer up later.

732310209.text: Ah, I misspeak. You, Pale Floater, are not as bold as my Yasnapati... But perhaps one may consider retreating at the slightest sign of danger a wise choice.

732310210.text: #Right... That's right! {NICKNAME}'s in charge of being brave, while Paimon's in charge of being smart. That's why we make the best of buddies, after all!

732310212.text: Hehe, right? Paimon thinks that was a good rejoinder too!

732310213.text: ... But I did not give you your title for naught, Yasnapati. Do give praise unto my bravery more, pray.

732310214.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}'s known Paimon longer. When {M#he's}{F#she's} not being your Yasnapati, there's nothing wrong with {M#him}{F#her} sparing some time to praise Paimon!

732310215.text: Anyway, don't sweat the small stuff, Sorush. You're not really doing anything that especially needs praising right now, are you...

732310216.text: My great work is not for the present, but the future. Still, at this very moment... you are being given the privilege to witness where it all begins!

732310217.text: Well, if you say so. Speaking of which, we're here to find...

732310218.text: Mihir. That foolish familiar of thorns... She must be suffering right now.

732310219.text: Wait. Is she trapped in there? Then we've got to go save her!

732310220.text: The power of the purple mist beneath us shares a source with the demons of Dev. Mihir's task should have been to keep such wicked powers from running rampant upon this earth.

732310221.text: Under the Sign of Apaosha, the powers of the two forces warring here ebb and flow...

732310222.text: We Pari should be dauntless, willing to fight till we ourselves are torn to shreds... but Mihir? Hah. I shouldn't wonder if she searches for some way to protect herself even now, conducting some loathsome struggle.

732310207.text: But don't you find that pretty suspicious already? Paimon can tell how dangerous it is just by looking!

732310401.text: Wait, is this Mihir? Is she... stuck? Seems like the purple mist has already made it all the way down here...

732310402.text: What do we do now, Sorush? Can we just do what we did earlier? Y'know, give some of your power to the thorns and free her?

732310403.text: Why of course, I shall save her. After all, she does seem so very piteous, infested with corruption and helpless as she is.

732310404.text: This isn't the best time to throw shade on her.

732310405.text: Exactly! We've got to save her, and quick...

732310406.text: Yet I have not heard her repent! I shall hear her repudiation of her obduracy and her supplication for my aid...

732310407.text: Oh, come on, are you serious? We don't have time for that kinda talk! Paimon thought you were just speaking in anger...

732310412.text: Well, then... If you, too, say so, my Yasnapati. After all, fulfilling your wishes once in a while is indeed within the purview of one so exalted as I.

732310413.text: Eh!? Seriously? Paimon wishes you'd listen to her too, Sorush...

732310805.text: Sorush, Sorush... Sorush who took humans for companions. Sorush who lost her way.

732310806.text: Uhh... It sounds like there's some secret meaning behind her words...

732310807.text: Do not get near her, lest the defilement that emanates from her touches you...

732310808.text: It seems that she has not only forgone a heart of gratitude, but has lost much of her intellect, or she would not use such baseless words to reproach me.

732310809.text: Thank you, Sorush. If not for you and your companions, I would have needed much time to gather my strength...

732310810.text: And even then, I am unsure if I could have stood against the rising filth on my own.

732310811.text: The Sign of Apaosha could be seen all too clearly, even from the bottom of the valley, but thorns can only crawl upon the ground, never to reach the sky — not even the reflection of the skies on the earth...

732310812.text: Hmph. Of course. After all, I am the one who is destined to make sacrifices and extinguish the Sign.

732310813.text: #And I must add that {NICKNAME} is no companion of mine, nor is Paimon. {M#He}{F#She} is my Yasnapati, a willing instrument recording my great work.

732311103.text: We won't be able to relax till we manage to fix the crisis above us.

732311104.text: That's true, but let's prioritize escorting Mihir on her cleansing pilgrimage so she can regain her spotless form and return to her companions' side.

732311105.text: But isn't it awful that she's been fighting all this time, but now that she's injured, she can't even go back...

732311106.text: One who clings to life and self-protection despite being filled with such filth is unworthy of a Yasnapati's chronicle.

732311107.text: What are you saying, Sorush? Mihir's been fighting all by herself to fulfill her mission all this time... She's been very brave.

732311108.text: We should remember what she's done and praise her for it!

732311109.text: Only humans require such things as courage. We Pari have no need of it.

732311110.text: Sorush speaks the truth. We Pari have known our purpose since birth, and we only live to serve that purpose. We do not require remembrance.

732311111.text: Perhaps being forgotten might even be for the best.

732311113.text: If the day comes when none mention us again, then surely the entire earth must have been purged of all calamity.

732311114.text: There will be no more sacrifices to be sung of, for there will be no more sufferings to be remembered.

732311115.text: I believe that that shall be a wonderful day.

732311117.text: That day is yet distant. Not before I make the sacrifice that shall extinguish the Sign of Apaosha, at least...

732311118.text: Let us not waste daylight here. We should complete the cleansing pilgrimage as soon as possible.

732311119.text: We should not allow this preamble to delay us so... I am the protagonist of this hymn... I alone...

732311120.text: Thank you for walking this difficult path with me. I believe that the road shall be far smoother ahead. Would you like us to continue on together?

732311122.text: Yes. You know where to find me.

732311124.text: That is also fine by me.

732311201.text: We're back! Guess your cleansing pilgrimage is done, huh, Mihir? And that means your "defilement" issues have been solved, right?

732311202.text: I have indeed completed the cleansing pilgrimage, but it couldn't have been done without your aid.

732311203.text: The wind and waters here are good, and wondrous energies cycle here. For now, there is no need to worry about the defilement.

732311204.text: Yeah, this place sure is better than that valley full of purple mist. It's definitely got that... "soul-purifying" feeling to it.

732311206.text: Hehehe, that was easier than Paimon thought! Now that Mihir's clear of this "defilement," other Pari aren't gonna reject her anymore, right?

732311207.text: You can finally take a rest after all that trouble you went through, Mihir.

732311208.text: And Sorush is now closer to obtaining the Chaplet as well.

732311210.text: A fitting end for Mihir, perhaps, but not for me.

732311211.text: My ending will not be something so ordinary or peaceful... or as insignificant as you are, Pale Floater.

732311212.text: Paimon isn't insignificant! ... Well, not that Paimon's very heavy or anything either!

732311213.text: My end shall be glorious, radiant, like that of the divine bird Simurgh. I shall split into infinite motes of Khvarena, cleansing the world of its impurity...

732311214.text: That which Mihir has done cannot be compared to what I shall yet accomplish.

732311215.text: Yet there was only one Simurgh, and there is only one Sorush.

732311217.text: My Yasnapati, it is clear that you do not understand Simurgh's greatness. Nor do you rate the tragic vow and resolve of us Pari as you should.

732311220.text: You speak but empty words, born of your witlessness. My mind is made up, my heart set. I will not be moved.

732311221.text: Ugh, Paimon doesn't get Sorush at all. Why does she insist on sacrificing herself to deal with the Sign? And why is she so cold to Mihir?

732311219.text: Paimon thinks so too! You don't have to be in such a hurry to sacrifice yourself! We can think of something else together!

732310101.text: Um, uh... Are you sure we're going the right way, Sorush?

732310102.text: Stop making such disgraceful noises. Would I lead you wrong?

732310103.text: #Hmph. Pale Floater, you could stand to learn from our Yasnapati and {M#his}{F#her} unflinching calm.

732310105.text: Exactly! Just looking at that big mass of... stuff down there is pretty scary already...

732310108.text: Such trivial trials! They pale in comparison to the sacrifice that I must offer up later.

732310109.text: Ah, I misspeak. You, Pale Floater, are not as bold as my Yasnapati... But perhaps one may consider retreating at the slightest sign of danger a wise choice.

732310110.text: #Right... That's right! {NICKNAME}'s in charge of being brave, while Paimon's in charge of being smart. That's why we make the best of buddies, after all!

732310112.text: Hehe, right? Paimon thinks that was a good rejoinder too!

732310113.text: ... But I did not give you your title for naught, Yasnapati. Do give praise unto my bravery more, pray.

732310114.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}'s known Paimon longer. When {M#he's}{F#she's} not being your Yasnapati, there's nothing wrong with {M#him}{F#her} sparing some time to praise Paimon!

732310115.text: Anyway, don't sweat the small stuff, Sorush. You're not really doing anything that especially needs praising right now, are you...

732310116.text: My great work is not for the present, but the future. Still, at this very moment... you are being given the privilege to witness where it all begins!

732310117.text: Well, if you say so. Speaking of which, we're here to find...

732310118.text: Mihir. That foolish familiar of thorns... She must be suffering right now.

732310119.text: Wait. Is she trapped down there? Then we've got to go save her!

732310120.text: The power of the purple mist beneath us shares a source with the demons of Dev. Mihir's task should have been to keep such wicked powers from running rampant upon this earth.

732310121.text: Under the Sign of Apaosha, the powers of the two forces warring here ebb and flow...

732310122.text: We Pari should be dauntless, willing to fight till we ourselves are torn to shreds... but Mihir? Hah. I shouldn't wonder if she searches for some way to protect herself even now, conducting some loathsome struggle.

732310123.text: Wait. Aren't you allies? Are you really gonna leave a fellow Pari to her fate like that?

732310107.text: But don't you find that pretty suspicious already? Paimon can tell how dangerous it is just by looking!

732310601.text: Wait. Aren't you allies? Are you really gonna leave a fellow Pari to her fate like that?

732310603.text: Uh... Paimon can't tell if you're genuinely scolding her or not!

732310609.text: It is no difficult matter, saving Mihir. Perhaps I might even call it trivial. But we Pari each have our mission, and we also have different... ideals.

732310610.text: She must've found some position equal in seclusion and defensibility, before using a Gray Gate to seal both the demons and herself in.

732310611.text: If she could still move freely, aha, she would be like that Khvarena, begging for aid and prostrating herself before all and sundry to earn pity.

732310613.text: Maybe if they try hard enough?

732310614.text: You plebeians miss the point. All the same, the state of this place tells me that she shall not hold out long by herself. How pitiful...

732310615.text: Pah, what a horrible sight. To be as Mihir is, corroded by filth, falling from a spotless to a sinful state, yet desperate to preserve herself... Had the Elder not bade me come...

732310616.text: Hehe. So after all that, you do care!

732310617.text: Hardly! I merely wish to see if that useless fool has any regrets or not. If she turns back to us and accepts our aid, then perhaps I shall spare her a moment or two.

732310618.text: ...After all, the flower, the star of the songs of praise, shall seem less radiant if the green leaves are not there to serve as its foil.

732310619.text: The following labor shall be little, but it is still a radiant shard. Yasnapati mine, record it down with a reverent heart, and use even this mote of shattered light to grace your mighty hymn.

732310620.text: We can talk about the less important stuff later, Sorush. Let's figure out how to disperse that purple mist first!

732310621.text: "Less important," you say!? *sigh* ... Well, so be it.

732310622.text: Mihir's sinful form renders her unable to fulfill her duty, but the thorns remain. So long as I lend them some of my strength, it shall only take a brief moment to scatter this purple smoke.

732310623.text: As for the downward path, let us follow that wandering Khvarena we just saw.

732310624.text: Well, if Sorush's so sure... Let's try getting closer then!

732310625.text: Oh, right. If you feel uncomfortable, then hold your breath! Well, Paimon isn't all that good at doing that herself... so you'd better make it quick, Sorush!

732310605.text: Huh, maybe you're right. The problem could very well be something not even Sorush can solve.

732310607.text: That's right! They're like a big family, always protecting one another! So you Pari aren't like that, huh...

732310608.text: The Aranara? Hah. What a carefree breed.

732310701.text: Um, uh... Are you sure we're going the right way, Sorush? We seem to have been around these parts before...

732311719.text: Huh, Sorush, so the Pari you mentioned about was Mihir? Is she trapped down there? In that case, we've gotta go save her!

732311720.text: The power of the purple mist you witnessed previously and the demons of Dev stem from the same source. Mihir's task should have been to keep such wicked powers from running rampant upon this earth.

732311707.text: And how is that not annoying enough, huh?

732312101.text: Wait, is this Mihir? Is she... stuck? Seems like the purple mist has already made it all the way down here...

732312102.text: What do we do now, Sorush? Can we just do what we did earlier? Y'know, give some of your power to the thorns and free her?

732312103.text: Why of course, I shall save her. After all, she does seem so very piteous, infested with corruption and helpless as she is.

732312104.text: This isn't the best time to throw shade on her.

732312105.text: Exactly! We've got to save her, and quick...

732312106.text: Yet I have not heard her repent! I shall hear her repudiation of her obduracy and her supplication for my aid...

732312107.text: Oh, come on, are you serious? We don't have time for that kinda talk! Paimon thought you were just speaking in anger...

732312112.text: Well, then... If you, too, say so, my Yasnapati. After all, fulfilling your wishes once in a while is indeed within the purview of one so exalted as I.

732312113.text: Eh!? Seriously? Paimon wishes you'd listen to her too, Sorush...

732312202.text: Well, I suppose she is alive, if barely, and covered in sin, and weakened to the extent that she may only defend herself...

732312205.text: Sorush, Sorush... Sorush who took humans for companions. Sorush who lost her way.

732312206.text: Uhh... It sounds like there's some secret meaning behind her words...

732312207.text: Do not get near her, lest the defilement that emanates from her touches you...

732312208.text: It seems that she has not only forgone a heart of gratitude, but has lost much of her intellect, or she would not use such baseless words to reproach me.

732312209.text: Thank you, Sorush. If not for you and your companions, I would have needed much time to gather my strength...

732312210.text: And even then, I am unsure if I could have stood against the rising filth on my own.

732312211.text: The Sign of Apaosha could be seen all too clearly, even from the bottom of the valley, but thorns can only crawl upon the ground, never to reach the sky — not even the reflection of the skies on the earth...

732312212.text: Hmph. Of course. After all, I am the one who is destined to make sacrifices and extinguish the Sign.

732312213.text: #And I must add that {NICKNAME} is no companion of mine, nor is Paimon. {M#He}{F#She} is my Yasnapati, a willing instrument recording my great work.

732312401.text: We're back! Guess your cleansing pilgrimage is done, huh, Mihir? And that means your "defilement" issues have been solved, right?

732312402.text: The Vourukasha Oasis has wonderful winds and waters, and bountiful energies...

732312403.text: Yeah, this place sure is better than that valley full of purple mist. It's definitely got that... "soul-purifying" feeling to it.

732312405.text: Is that all? Well, that was easier than Paimon thought! Now that Mihir's clear of this "defilement," other Pari aren't gonna reject her anymore, right?

732312406.text: You can finally take a rest after all that trouble you went through, Mihir.

732312407.text: And Sorush is now closer to obtaining the Chaplet as well.

732312409.text: A fitting end for Mihir, perhaps, but not for me.

732312410.text: My ending will not be something so ordinary or peaceful... or as insignificant as you are, Pale Floater.

732312411.text: Paimon isn't insignificant! ... Well, not that Paimon's very heavy or anything either!

732312412.text: My end shall be glorious, radiant, like that of the divine bird Simurgh. I shall split into infinite motes of Khvarena, cleansing the world of its impurity...

732312413.text: That which Mihir has done cannot be compared to what I shall yet accomplish.

732312414.text: Yet there was only one Simurgh, and there is only one Sorush.

732312416.text: My Yasnapati, it is clear that you do not understand Simurgh's greatness. Nor do you rate the tragic vow and resolve of us Pari as you should.

732312419.text: You speak but empty words, born of your witlessness. My mind is made up, my heart set. I will not be moved.

732312420.text: Ugh, Paimon doesn't get Sorush at all. Why does she insist on sacrificing herself to deal with the Sign? And why is she so cold to Mihir?

732312418.text: Paimon thinks so too! You don't have to be in such a hurry to sacrifice yourself! We can think of something else together!

732312501.text: I will not require a Yasnapati. Sorush may desire human praise, but I do not need it.

732312502.text: Still, I'm grateful for this chance to return to the Vourukasha Oasis for a brief respite. Thank you.

732319907.text: Speaking of that, why didn't you help Mihir earlier, Sorush?

732319908.text: If you just lent a little power to the thorns, you could've done that even without our help, right?

732319909.text: This is my duty, not hers.

732319910.text: Eh? But shouldn't you help each other out at times like this?

732319911.text: Each Pari has their own mission, and just like this cleansing pilgrimage, we must undertake those tasks ourselves.

732319912.text: Missions and duties... all have someone they belong to, and we cannot allow others to take over completely.
